moodle_database::insert_record() converts its argument with (array)$dataobject in every driver (mysqli_native_moodle_database.php:1474, pgsql :1177, sqlsrv :1138), so passing the array literal instead of (object) inserts the same row and returns the same id.

insert_record() with returnid=true returns an int id in every driver (mysqli_native_moodle_database.php, pgsql, sqlsrv), so the (int) cast on the reassigned $connectionid changes nothing; it is equivalent only because of that driver contract, and the value only feeds the stored row and the event objectid.

Removing the (int) cast of the connection id passed to grant_active(int $id, int $userid): connection.php declares no strict_types, so a numeric string from the database is coerced to int by the typed target parameter, giving the identical int and the identical record_exists() query.
